# Cytoscape Web App Cookbook

> Task-oriented recipes for Cytoscape Web apps: one TypeScript function per
> task, with a header that says when to use it, what it changes, and what
> not to do. Each compiles against the published API types and passed a
> case in a running Cytoscape Web.

- Examples commit: `46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a`. Every link below is pinned to it.
- Verified on: Cytoscape Web 1.1.0 (`6619411b`) and Cytoscape Web 1.1.1 (`c3118c51`). Supported: 1.1.0 and later.
- API types: `@cytoscape-web/api-types@1.0.0-beta.5`.

---

# Using a recipe

A recipe is one TypeScript file that performs one task in Cytoscape Web, such as
"color nodes by a numeric column". It exports one function. Its header comment
says when to use it, what it changes, and what goes wrong.

This page is for developers and for coding agents. The index is
[README.md](README.md).

## 1. Find the recipe

Look in the index for the task in the user's own words. The "Also asked as"
column lists them: "heat map" and "color by score" both lead to
`style/color-nodes-by-numeric-column`.

If no recipe fits, do not adapt one by guessing. Read the
[API reference](https://github.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web/blob/development/src/app-api/api_docs/Api.md)
and let the type checker tell you what exists.

## 2. Copy it into your app

Copy the file as it is, for example to `src/recipes/`, and import its function.

- Keep the header. It is the documentation.
- Keep the imports as they are: `import type { … } from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'`.
  They are types only. `@cytoscape-web/api-types` ships declarations and no
  code, so importing a value from it (`ok`, `fail`, `VisualPropertyName`)
  compiles and then fails in the browser.
- A recipe imports nothing else, so one file is all you need.

## 3. Give it `apis`

Every recipe takes `apis` as its first argument. Where `apis` comes from
depends on where you call the recipe. [`wiring/`](wiring) has one compiled
example per call site.

| You are in | `apis` is | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `mount(context)` | `context.apis` | [`wiring/from-mount.ts`](wiring/from-mount.ts) |
| the `onClick` of an `'apps-menu'` entry | the `apis` parameter | [`wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`](wiring/from-apps-menu.ts) |
| a React component | `useAppContext()?.apis`, or the `use*Api` hooks | [`wiring/from-panel.tsx`](wiring/from-panel.tsx) |
| a script that is not an app | `await window.CyWebApi.whenReady()` | [`wiring/from-window.ts`](wiring/from-window.ts) |

**Look at the type of the recipe's `apis` parameter.** It decides which of
these you may use.

- `Pick<CyWebApiType, …>` is a **host-wide** recipe. Any of the four works.
- `Pick<AppContextApis, …>` is an **owner-bound** recipe. It uses `resource`,
  `dialog`, `appData`, `contextMenu`, `nodeGraphics` or `panel`, which belong
  to one app. Pass it only `context.apis`, the `onClick` parameter, or
  `useAppContext()?.apis`. **Never `window.CyWebApi`, and never a `use*Api`
  hook.** The types accept them, and the result is wrong: what the recipe
  registers is not removed when the app is disabled, and `panel.open` may
  select another app's tab.

## 4. Check the result

A recipe returns `ApiResult<T>` (a `Promise` of one where the API is
asynchronous). It does not throw.

```typescript
const colored = colorNodesByNumericColumn(apis, networkId, 'score')
if (!colored.success) {
  console.error(colored.error.code, colored.error.message)
  return
}
console.info(`colored ${colored.data.mappedCount} nodes`)
```

A failure is either the host's own, passed on unchanged, or the recipe's. A
recipe's own codes start with `RECIPE_` and are listed in its header.

## 5. Know when the host is ready

Four different things are easy to take for one.

1. **`window.CyWebApi` exists.** It does before the host has finished
   starting. Do not call it yet.
2. **The API is ready.** `await window.CyWebApi.whenReady()`. Inside an app
   this has already happened.
3. **A network's data is loaded.** This is per network. After a page reload,
   `network:switched` arrives before the network's tables do, and a read made
   then fails with `APP1`. Use
   [`events/follow-current-network`](recipes/events/follow-current-network.ts).
4. **Your app is active.** The host calls `mount()`, waits for it to return,
   and only then shows the app's panels and dialogs. So `mount()` must never
   wait for the app's own UI.

## 6. What "verified" means

[`verified.json`](verified.json) records what the recipes were checked with:

- the `@cytoscape-web/api-types` version every file compiles against, with
  library checking on;
- the Cytoscape Web releases on which every recipe's case passed, in a real
  host. The cookbook supports **Cytoscape Web 1.1.0 and later**, and is run on
  1.1.0 and on the latest release.

Where the releases behave differently, the recipe's header says so by version.
If your host is older than 1.1.0, or runs a build that is not a release,
nothing here was checked against it.

## 7. The shortest way to see one work

```bash
npm create cytoscape-app my-app
cd my-app
```

Copy a recipe to `src/recipes/`, call it from the `onClick` in
`src/menuActions.ts`, then:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open the install link the dev server prints, confirm the install, open a
network, and choose your entry in the **Apps** menu.

## Rules for a coding agent

- Use the recipe's function. Do not rewrite it from memory.
- If the type checker rejects a name, that name does not exist. Do not cast
  your way past it.
- Do not invent visual property names, event names or error codes. They are
  string literals that the types check.
- Read the "Don't" section of the recipe before you change anything in it.

---

# Wiring

## cookbook/wiring/from-apps-menu.ts

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/wiring/from-apps-menu.ts

````typescript
/**
 * Call site 2 of 4: the `onClick` of an `'apps-menu'` entry.
 *
 * The host passes this app's own API object to `onClick`. Like
 * `context.apis`, it has every domain, including the owner-bound ones.
 *
 * A menu entry is plain data: it has no component. An action that needs a
 * form or a progress display opens it with `apis.dialog.open(...)`.
 */
import type { ResourceDeclaration } from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

import { addNodesToNetwork } from '../recipes/elements/add-nodes-to-network'
import { colorNodesByNumericColumn } from '../recipes/style/color-nodes-by-numeric-column'

export const menuEntries: ResourceDeclaration[] = [
  {
    slot: 'apps-menu',
    id: 'AddChain',
    label: 'Add a chain of three nodes',
    requires: { network: true },
    onClick: (apis) => {
      const current = apis.workspace.getCurrentNetworkId()
      if (!current.success) return

      const added = addNodesToNetwork(
        apis,
        current.data.networkId,
        [{ name: 'A' }, { name: 'B' }, { name: 'C' }],
        [
          [0, 1],
          [1, 2],
        ],
      )
      if (!added.success) console.error(added.error.message)
    },
  },
  {
    slot: 'apps-menu',
    id: 'ColorByScore',
    label: 'Color nodes by score',
    requires: { network: true },
    onClick: (apis) => {
      const current = apis.workspace.getCurrentNetworkId()
      if (!current.success) return

      const colored = colorNodesByNumericColumn(
        apis,
        current.data.networkId,
        'score',
      )
      if (!colored.success) console.error(colored.error.message)
    },
  },
]
````

## cookbook/wiring/from-mount.ts

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/wiring/from-mount.ts

````typescript
/**
 * Call site 1 of 4: `mount(context)` and `unmount()`.
 *
 * `context.apis` is this app's own API object. It has every domain, including
 * the owner-bound ones (`resource`, `dialog`, `appData`, `contextMenu`,
 * `nodeGraphics`, `panel`), so every recipe can be called from here.
 *
 * `mount()` must return without waiting for the app's own panel or dialog:
 * the host shows them only after `mount()` has returned.
 */
import type { AppContext, CyAppWithLifecycle, IdType } from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

import { followCurrentNetwork } from '../recipes/events/follow-current-network'

let stopFollowing: (() => void) | null = null

export const lifecycle: Pick<CyAppWithLifecycle, 'mount' | 'unmount'> = {
  mount(context: AppContext): void {
    const read = (networkId: IdType): boolean => {
      const nodes = context.apis.element.getNodeIds(networkId)
      // false: the data has not arrived yet, so the recipe reads again when
      // it does.
      if (!nodes.success) return false
      console.info(`${networkId} has ${nodes.data.nodeIds.length} nodes`)
      return true
    }

    const following = followCurrentNetwork(context.apis, read, () => {
      console.info('no network is open')
    })
    if (following.success) stopFollowing = following.data.stop
  },

  unmount(): void {
    stopFollowing?.()
    stopFollowing = null
  },
}
````

## cookbook/wiring/from-panel.tsx

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/wiring/from-panel.tsx

````typescript
/**
 * Call site 3 of 4: a React component, such as a `'right-panel'` panel.
 *
 * Two sources, for two kinds of domain:
 *
 * - **Host-wide domains** (`element`, `network`, `selection`, `viewport`,
 *   `table`, `visualStyle`, `layout`, `export`, `workspace`): the `use*Api`
 *   hooks, one per domain.
 * - **Owner-bound domains** (`resource`, `dialog`, `appData`, `contextMenu`,
 *   `nodeGraphics`, `panel`): `useAppContext()?.apis`, and nothing else. A
 *   recipe that needs one of them takes that object.
 *
 * To follow the current network in a component, read it once when the
 * component mounts, then on its events through the `useCyWebEvent` hook, which
 * subscribes on mount and unsubscribes on unmount. Clear what you show when no
 * network is current.
 */
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from 'react'

import { useAppContext } from 'cyweb/AppIdContext'
import { useElementApi } from 'cyweb/ElementApi'
import { useCyWebEvent } from 'cyweb/EventBus'
import { useViewportApi } from 'cyweb/ViewportApi'
import { useWorkspaceApi } from 'cyweb/WorkspaceApi'

import { addNodesToNetwork } from '../recipes/elements/add-nodes-to-network'
import { colorNodesByNumericColumn } from '../recipes/style/color-nodes-by-numeric-column'

const ExamplePanel = (): JSX.Element => {
  // Host-wide domains, from their hooks.
  const element = useElementApi()
  const viewport = useViewportApi()
  const workspace = useWorkspaceApi()
  // This app's own API object. It is null outside an app's own tree.
  const apis = useAppContext()?.apis

  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')
  const [nodeCount, setNodeCount] = useState<number | null>(null)

  // Always show the network that is current now, whatever event asked.
  // No network, or one whose data has not arrived yet, shows nothing.
  const readNodeCount = useCallback((): void => {
    const current = workspace.getCurrentNetworkId()
    if (!current.success) {
      setNodeCount(null)
      return
    }
    const nodes = element.getNodeIds(current.data.networkId)
    setNodeCount(nodes.success ? nodes.data.nodeIds.length : null)
  }, [element, workspace])

  // 1. When the panel opens: a network may already be on screen, and no
  //    event will announce it.
  useEffect(() => {
    readNodeCount()
  }, [readNodeCount])
  // 2. On every switch, including to no network at all (an empty id).
  useCyWebEvent('network:switched', readNodeCount)
  // 3. When data arrives: a read made on the switch alone can fail with APP1.
  useCyWebEvent('network:loaded', readNodeCount)
  // 4. When nodes or edges are added or removed: by this panel's own button,
  //    by another app, or by Edit ▸ Undo.
  useCyWebEvent('network:changed', readNodeCount)

  const addChain = (): void => {
    const current = workspace.getCurrentNetworkId()
    if (!current.success) {
      setMessage(current.error.message)
      return
    }
    const added = addNodesToNetwork(
      { element, viewport },
      current.data.networkId,
      [{ name: 'A' }, { name: 'B' }, { name: 'C' }],
      [
        [0, 1],
        [1, 2],
      ],
    )
    setMessage(
      added.success
        ? `Added ${added.data.nodeIds.length} nodes`
        : added.error.message,
    )
  }

  // The app's own API object has every domain, so it serves a host-wide
  // recipe too. A recipe typed Pick<AppContextApis, …> accepts only this.
  const colorByScore = (): void => {
    if (apis === undefined) return
    const current = apis.workspace.getCurrentNetworkId()
    if (!current.success) {
      setMessage(current.error.message)
      return
    }
    const colored = colorNodesByNumericColumn(
      apis,
      current.data.networkId,
      'score',
    )
    setMessage(
      colored.success
        ? `Colored ${colored.data.mappedCount} nodes`
        : colored.error.message,
    )
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <p>{nodeCount === null ? 'No network' : `${nodeCount} nodes`}</p>
      <button onClick={addChain}>Add a chain of three nodes</button>
      <button onClick={colorByScore}>Color nodes by score</button>
      <p>{message}</p>
    </div>
  )
}

export default ExamplePanel
````

## cookbook/wiring/from-window.ts

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/wiring/from-window.ts

````typescript
/**
 * Call site 4 of 4: `window.CyWebApi`, from code that is not an app.
 *
 * Use it from a script on the page, a bookmarklet or a test. Two limits:
 *
 * - **Wait for `whenReady()`.** `window.CyWebApi` exists before the host has
 *   finished starting, and its methods may not work until then.
 * - **Host-wide domains only.** `window.CyWebApi` has no `resource`, `dialog`
 *   or `appData`. Its `contextMenu`, `nodeGraphics` and `panel` belong to no
 *   app: what they register is not removed when an app is disabled. Never
 *   pass it to a recipe that takes `Pick<AppContextApis, …>`.
 */
import type { ApiResult } from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

import {
  addNodesToNetwork,
  type AddedElements,
} from '../recipes/elements/add-nodes-to-network'

export async function addChainFromPage(): Promise<ApiResult<AddedElements>> {
  const api = await window.CyWebApi.whenReady()

  const current = api.workspace.getCurrentNetworkId()
  if (!current.success) return current

  return addNodesToNetwork(
    api,
    current.data.networkId,
    [{ name: 'A' }, { name: 'B' }, { name: 'C' }],
    [
      [0, 1],
      [1, 2],
    ],
  )
}
````

# Recipes

## Add a computed column: node degree

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/data/add-computed-column.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Add a computed column: node degree
 * @aliases add a column, computed column, calculate degree, node degree,
 *   number of connections, count neighbors, derived attribute, write
 *   results to the table
 * @apis element.getNodeIds, element.getEdges, table.getColumns,
 *   table.createColumn, table.setValues, table.deleteColumn
 * @related data/read-column-values-safely, style/size-nodes-by-degree,
 *   data/join-table-by-key
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user asks for a value computed from the network to be added to the
 * node table, here each node's degree, so that it can be sorted, filtered or
 * mapped to a style. Replace the computation to write anything else.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 * - No node column has the chosen name in another type, or in another
 *   spelling of the same letters.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Creates an `integer` column named `column` (default `degree`) when there
 *   is none, and writes every node's value in one batch.
 * - Writing the values records **one** undo entry. Creating the column
 *   records none: after an undo the column stays, holding its previous
 *   values (`0` for a new one).
 * - If writing fails, the recipe deletes the column it created. Deleting a
 *   column records an undo entry of its own.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Read the topology once.** `getEdges` returns every edge with its ends.
 *   One `getConnectedEdges` call per node does the same work node by node.
 * - **A self-loop counts twice**, as in Cytoscape Desktop.
 * - **Use the batch call.** One `setValues` validates every value first and
 *   writes all or nothing. A loop of `setValue` records one undo entry per
 *   node and can stop halfway.
 * - **Column names and case.** 1.1.0 compares column names exactly and would
 *   create `degree` next to an existing `Degree`; 1.1.1 compares them
 *   ignoring case and refuses it with `AC6`. The recipe checks itself and
 *   refuses such a name on both, before changing anything.
 * - **Running it again updates the column** when it is `integer` or `long`.
 *   A column of that name in another type is refused.
 * - **The column is a snapshot.** It does not follow later edits to the
 *   network: run the recipe again after adding or deleting edges.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't create the column with a type the values do not have: a degree is
 *   a whole number, and `setValues` refuses `2.5` in an `integer` column.
 * - Don't name the column `id`: the host refuses it.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CellEdit,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface ComputedColumn {
  column: string
  /** Whether the recipe created the column, or updated an existing one. */
  created: boolean
  min: number
  max: number
}

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function addDegreeColumn(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'element' | 'table'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  column = 'degree',
): ApiResult<ComputedColumn> {
  const nodes = apis.element.getNodeIds(networkId)
  if (!nodes.success) return nodes
  const edges = apis.element.getEdges(networkId)
  if (!edges.success) return edges

  // Compute first: nothing is written until the values exist.
  const degree = new Map<IdType, number>()
  for (const id of nodes.data.nodeIds) degree.set(id, 0)
  for (const edge of edges.data.edges) {
    degree.set(edge.sourceId, (degree.get(edge.sourceId) ?? 0) + 1)
    degree.set(edge.targetId, (degree.get(edge.targetId) ?? 0) + 1)
  }

  const columns = apis.table.getColumns(networkId, 'node')
  if (!columns.success) return columns
  const same = columns.data.columns.find(
    (c) => c.name.toLowerCase() === column.toLowerCase(),
  )
  if (same !== undefined && same.name !== column) {
    return failure(
      'RECIPE_NAME_CLASH',
      `a column named ${same.name} exists; choose a name that differs by ` +
        `more than case`,
    )
  }
  if (same !== undefined && same.type !== 'integer' && same.type !== 'long') {
    return failure(
      'RECIPE_COLUMN_TYPE',
      `${column} exists as a ${same.type} column`,
    )
  }

  const created = same === undefined
  if (created) {
    const made = apis.table.createColumn(networkId, 'node', column, 'integer', 0)
    if (!made.success) return made
  }

  const edits: CellEdit[] = []
  let min = Infinity
  let max = -Infinity
  for (const [id, value] of degree) {
    edits.push({ id, column, value })
    min = Math.min(min, value)
    max = Math.max(max, value)
  }
  const written = apis.table.setValues(networkId, 'node', edits)
  if (!written.success) {
    if (created) apis.table.deleteColumn(networkId, 'node', column)
    return written
  }

  return {
    success: true,
    data: { column, created, min: edits.length ? min : 0, max: edits.length ? max : 0 },
  }
}
````

## Join a table of values to the network by a key column

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/data/join-table-by-key.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Join a table of values to the network by a key column
 * @aliases import table, import data, join table, merge data, add
 *   attributes from a file, import TSV, load node attributes, map data onto
 *   nodes, attribute table
 * @apis table.getColumns, table.importTableFromTsv
 * @related data/add-computed-column, data/read-column-values-safely,
 *   network/create-network-from-table
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user has a tab-separated table, such as expression values per gene,
 * and asks to attach it to the network's nodes (or edges) by a shared key:
 * Cytoscape's "Import Table From File".
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The first line names the columns. The key column holds the same values as
 *   a column of the network's table, such as `name`, or the element ids
 *   (key `id`).
 * - Values contain no tabs and no line breaks: the host does not read
 *   quotes.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Creates every column of the file that the table lacks, and writes the
 *   values of every row whose key matches.
 * - Records **no** undo entry: Edit ▸ Undo does not remove imported data.
 * - A row whose key matches nothing is skipped and reported in
 *   `unmatchedKeys`. A key that matches several elements, two nodes with the
 *   same `name`, writes to all of them.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Give each column a type in the header**, as Cytoscape Desktop does:
 *   `score:double`. Without one the host infers the type from the first few
 *   rows, and a later value that does not fit is skipped and reported in
 *   `skippedCells`.
 * - **Line endings.** A file saved on Windows ends its lines with `\r\n`,
 *   and the host splits on `\n` alone: every last value would end in `\r`.
 *   The recipe converts the line endings first.
 * - **Column names and case.** 1.1.0 matches a file column to a table column
 *   by its exact name, and would create `Score` next to an existing `score`;
 *   1.1.1 matches ignoring case and writes `Score` into `score`. The recipe
 *   refuses such a file on both, before changing anything.
 * - **An empty cell** leaves a number or boolean as it was, and writes an
 *   empty string into a text column.
 * - **Duplicate keys in the file** would leave the last row's values. The
 *   recipe refuses them.
 * - **A typed header must match an existing column's type.** 1.1.0 would
 *   write `score:long` values into a `double` column as they are; 1.1.1
 *   refuses them with `A1`. The recipe refuses such a file on both.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't loop over the rows with `setValue`: the import resolves the keys,
 *   creates the columns and writes everything in one call.
 * - Don't parse the file yourself to map names to node ids: pass `keyColumn`.
 * - Don't write CSV: the host reads tabs only.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  AppTableType,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface Joined {
  /** Elements that received values. */
  matchedElements: number
  /** Key values in the file that match no element. */
  unmatchedKeys: string[]
  /** Columns the import created. */
  newColumns: string[]
  /** Values that could not be read as their column's type. */
  skippedCells: Array<{ key: string; column: string; value: string }>
}

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

const TYPES = [
  'string', 'long', 'integer', 'double', 'boolean', 'list_of_string',
  'list_of_long', 'list_of_integer', 'list_of_double', 'list_of_boolean',
]

/**
 * A header field is `name` or `name:type`. As in the host, only a known type
 * after the last colon is one: `time:sec` is a column named `time:sec`.
 */
const columnName = (field: string): string => {
  const colon = field.lastIndexOf(':')
  return colon > 0 && TYPES.includes(field.slice(colon + 1))
    ? field.slice(0, colon)
    : field
}

export function joinTableByKey(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'table'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  tsvText: string,
  key: string,
  tableType: AppTableType = 'node',
): ApiResult<Joined> {
  const text = tsvText.replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n')
  const lines = text.split('\n').filter((line) => line.trim() !== '')
  if (lines.length < 2) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_ROWS', 'the file has no row under its header')
  }
  const header = lines[0].split('\t').map(columnName)
  const keyIndex = header.indexOf(key)
  if (keyIndex === -1) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_KEY_IN_FILE', `the file has no ${key} column`)
  }

  const columns = apis.table.getColumns(networkId, tableType)
  if (!columns.success) return columns
  if (key !== 'id' && !columns.data.columns.some((c) => c.name === key)) {
    return failure(
      'RECIPE_NO_KEY_COLUMN',
      `the ${tableType} table has no ${key} column to match`,
    )
  }

  // Same letters, other case: 1.1.0 and 1.1.1 would do different things.
  const seen = new Map<string, string>()
  for (const name of [...columns.data.columns.map((c) => c.name), ...header]) {
    const other = seen.get(name.toLowerCase())
    if (other !== undefined && other !== name) {
      return failure(
        'RECIPE_NAME_CLASH',
        `${name} and ${other} differ only by case`,
      )
    }
    seen.set(name.toLowerCase(), name)
  }
  if (new Set(header).size !== header.length) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NAME_CLASH', 'the file names a column twice')
  }

  // A typed header field for an existing column must keep its type: 1.1.0
  // would write the values as the file's type, and 1.1.1 refuses them (A1).
  for (const field of lines[0].split('\t')) {
    const name = columnName(field)
    const declared = field.slice(name.length + 1)
    const existing = columns.data.columns.find((c) => c.name === name)
    if (declared !== '' && existing !== undefined && existing.type !== declared) {
      return failure(
        'RECIPE_COLUMN_TYPE',
        `the file declares ${name} as ${declared}, and the table holds it ` +
          `as ${existing.type}`,
      )
    }
  }

  const keys = new Set<string>()
  for (const line of lines.slice(1)) {
    const value = line.split('\t')[keyIndex] ?? ''
    if (keys.has(value)) {
      return failure('RECIPE_DUPLICATE_KEY', `the key ${value} appears twice`)
    }
    keys.add(value)
  }

  const imported = apis.table.importTableFromTsv(
    networkId,
    tableType,
    lines.join('\n'),
    { keyColumn: key },
  )
  if (!imported.success) return imported
  return {
    success: true,
    data: {
      matchedElements: imported.data.rowCount,
      unmatchedKeys: imported.data.skippedRows,
      newColumns: imported.data.newColumns,
      skippedCells: imported.data.skippedCells,
    },
  }
}
````

## Read a column's numbers safely

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/data/read-column-values-safely.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Read a column's numbers safely
 * @aliases read column values, get numeric values, read a column, column to
 *   numbers, parse numbers from a column, column statistics, min and max of
 *   a column, missing values
 * @apis table.getTable
 * @related data/add-computed-column, style/color-nodes-by-numeric-column,
 *   style/emphasize-by-threshold
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * An app needs the numbers in a node or edge column, for a chart, a
 * statistic, a threshold or a mapping, and must not be fooled by missing,
 * textual or odd values.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - None. The recipe only reads.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Missing values.** A row with no value for the column, or an empty
 *   string, is reported in `missing`, not read as `0`.
 * - **A default is not missing.** A column created with a default value
 *   (`createColumn(…, 0)`) holds that value in every row it was not given
 *   another one. The table cannot tell the two apart.
 * - **Non-numeric values.** In a `double`, `long` or `integer` column every
 *   value is a number; `NaN` and the infinities are reported in `invalid`.
 *   In a `string` column the recipe parses each value strictly (`"1.5"` and
 *   `"2e3"` are numbers, `"1.5 kg"` and `"n/a"` are not) and reports what
 *   does not parse in `invalid`. `fromText` says that parsing happened.
 *   Boolean and list columns are refused.
 * - **An empty column** gives `range: null`. Check it before dividing by the
 *   width of the range.
 * - **All values equal** gives `min === max`. A gradient or a scale needs at
 *   least two different values.
 * - **Find the range with a loop.** `Math.min(...values)` passes one argument
 *   per row and throws a `RangeError` past about 120,000 of them.
 * - Ids come from the table's `id` field, which `getTable` adds by default.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't use `Number(value)` on its own: `Number('')` is `0` and
 *   `Number(null)` is `0`.
 * - Don't use `parseFloat`: `parseFloat('1.5 kg')` is `1.5`.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  AppTableType,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface NumericColumn {
  /** The column's declared type. */
  type: string
  /** Every finite number, by element id. */
  values: Record<IdType, number>
  /** Elements with no value. */
  missing: IdType[]
  /** Elements whose value is not a finite number. */
  invalid: IdType[]
  /** Whether the values were parsed from a text column. */
  fromText: boolean
  /** Null when no element has a number. */
  range: { min: number; max: number } | null
}

const NUMERIC_TYPES = ['double', 'long', 'integer']
const NUMBER_TEXT = /^\s*[-+]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][-+]?\d+)?\s*$/

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function readNumericColumn(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'table'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  tableType: AppTableType,
  column: string,
): ApiResult<NumericColumn> {
  const table = apis.table.getTable(networkId, tableType, {
    columns: [column],
  })
  if (!table.success) return table
  const info = table.data.columns.find((c) => c.name === column)
  if (info === undefined) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_COLUMN', `no ${tableType} column ${column}`)
  }
  const fromText = info.type === 'string'
  if (!fromText && !NUMERIC_TYPES.includes(info.type)) {
    return failure(
      'RECIPE_COLUMN_TYPE',
      `${column} is a ${info.type} column, which holds no numbers`,
    )
  }

  const result: NumericColumn = {
    type: info.type,
    values: {},
    missing: [],
    invalid: [],
    fromText,
    range: null,
  }
  let min = Infinity
  let max = -Infinity
  for (const row of table.data.rows) {
    const id = String(row.id)
    const raw = row[column]
    if (raw === undefined || raw === null || raw === '') {
      result.missing.push(id)
      continue
    }
    const value =
      typeof raw === 'number'
        ? raw
        : typeof raw === 'string' && NUMBER_TEXT.test(raw)
          ? Number(raw)
          : NaN
    if (!Number.isFinite(value)) {
      result.invalid.push(id)
      continue
    }
    result.values[id] = value
    min = Math.min(min, value)
    max = Math.max(max, value)
  }
  if (min !== Infinity) result.range = { min, max }
  return { success: true, data: result }
}
````

## Connect the selected nodes to each other

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/elements/add-edges-between-selected.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Connect the selected nodes to each other
 * @aliases add edges between selected nodes, connect selected nodes, link
 *   selected nodes, make a clique, connect all pairs, fully connect
 *   selection
 * @apis selection.getSelection, element.getEdges, element.createEdges
 * @related elements/add-nodes-to-network, elements/delete-selected,
 *   selection/select-neighbors
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user has selected some nodes and asks to connect them: every pair of
 * selected nodes gets an edge, unless it already has one.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - At least two nodes of `networkId` are selected.
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Adds one edge for each pair of selected nodes that no edge connects yet,
 *   in either direction. The source is the node selected first, in the order
 *   the host reports the selection.
 * - Records **one** undo entry for all the new edges.
 * - Does not change the selection, and adds no edge when every pair is
 *   already connected.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **The number of pairs grows with the square of the selection.** 50 nodes
 *   make up to 1,225 edges. The recipe refuses more than `maxEdges` (100 by
 *   default) before creating anything.
 * - **Use the batch call.** `createEdges` validates every edge first, creates
 *   all or none, and records one undo entry. A loop over `createEdge` records
 *   one per edge and can stop halfway. A failure here therefore leaves
 *   nothing behind.
 * - **Existing edges are read once**, with `getEdges`, not with one
 *   `getConnectedEdges` call per node.
 * - **`autoSelect` defaults to true** in the host. Left at the default, the
 *   new edges would replace the selection. The recipe passes `false`.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't connect the selected nodes in a chain when the user asked for them
 *   to be connected to each other, or the reverse.
 * - Don't add an edge where one already exists, unless the user asks for
 *   parallel edges.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface ConnectOptions {
  /** Refuse to create more edges than this. Defaults to 100. */
  maxEdges?: number
}

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

const pairKey = (a: IdType, b: IdType): string =>
  a < b ? `${a}\u0000${b}` : `${b}\u0000${a}`

export function addEdgesBetweenSelected(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'selection' | 'element'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  options: ConnectOptions = {},
): ApiResult<{ edgeIds: IdType[] }> {
  const selection = apis.selection.getSelection(networkId)
  if (!selection.success) return selection
  const nodes = selection.data.selectedNodes
  if (nodes.length < 2) {
    return failure('RECIPE_TOO_FEW_NODES', 'select at least two nodes')
  }

  const existing = apis.element.getEdges(networkId)
  if (!existing.success) return existing
  const connected = new Set(
    existing.data.edges.map((e) => pairKey(e.sourceId, e.targetId)),
  )

  const pairs: Array<[IdType, IdType]> = []
  for (let i = 0; i < nodes.length; i += 1) {
    for (let j = i + 1; j < nodes.length; j += 1) {
      if (!connected.has(pairKey(nodes[i], nodes[j]))) {
        pairs.push([nodes[i], nodes[j]])
      }
    }
  }
  const maxEdges = options.maxEdges ?? 100
  if (pairs.length > maxEdges) {
    return failure(
      'RECIPE_TOO_MANY_EDGES',
      `${pairs.length} edges would be created, more than ${maxEdges}`,
    )
  }
  if (pairs.length === 0) return { success: true, data: { edgeIds: [] } }

  const created = apis.element.createEdges(
    networkId,
    pairs.map(([sourceNodeId, targetNodeId]) => ({
      sourceNodeId,
      targetNodeId,
    })),
    { autoSelect: false },
  )
  if (!created.success) return created
  return {
    success: true,
    data: { edgeIds: created.data.edges.map((e) => e.edgeId) },
  }
}
````

## Add nodes to a network, and connect them

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/elements/add-nodes-to-network.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Add nodes to a network, and connect them
 * @aliases add nodes, create nodes, insert nodes, new nodes, add a chain of
 *   nodes, connect nodes, add edges between new nodes
 * @apis viewport.getNodePositions, element.createNodes, element.createEdges
 * @related style/color-nodes-by-numeric-column, events/follow-current-network
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user asks to add one or more nodes to an existing network, with or
 * without edges between the new nodes: "add three nodes A, B and C and connect
 * them in a chain".
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The network's data is loaded. A network that has just become current may
 *   not be readable yet; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 * - Each `link` is a pair of indexes into `nodes`: `[0, 1]` connects the first
 *   new node to the second.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Adds the nodes, each with its `name` and any other `attributes`.
 * - Adds one edge per link.
 * - Records one undo entry for all the nodes and, when there are links, a
 *   second one for all the edges. The user then undoes twice to remove
 *   everything.
 * - Does not change the selection.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Use the batch calls.** `createNodes` validates every node before it
 *   creates any, and records one undo entry. A loop over `createNode` records
 *   one entry per node and can stop halfway.
 * - **Every node needs a position.** Nodes created at the same position sit
 *   on top of each other. This recipe puts the new nodes in a row below the
 *   existing ones.
 * - **Find the extent with a loop.** `Math.min(...xs)` passes one argument
 *   per node, and throws a `RangeError` past about 120,000 of them. The host
 *   does not stop a network of that size from loading.
 * - **If the edges fail, the nodes stay.** The two batches are separate
 *   calls. The recipe returns the failure and leaves the nodes in place; one
 *   undo removes them. That cannot happen for a link that names a missing
 *   node, because the links are checked before anything is created.
 * - **`autoSelect` defaults to true** in the host. Left at the default, the
 *   new nodes replace the user's selection. This recipe passes `false`.
 * - An attribute must not be named `id`. The host assigns ids; read them from
 *   the result.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't invent node ids, and don't guess them from `generateNextNodeId`:
 *   use the ids that `createNodes` returns.
 * - Don't call `createNode` in a loop.
 * - Don't create edges before the nodes exist.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
  ValueType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface NewNode {
  /** Shown as the node's label in a network created by the host. */
  name: string
  /** Other columns to fill. Must not contain `id`. */
  attributes?: Record<string, ValueType>
}

export interface AddedElements {
  /** Ids of the created nodes, in the order of `nodes`. */
  nodeIds: IdType[]
  /** Ids of the created edges, in the order of `links`. */
  edgeIds: IdType[]
}

const SPACING = 120

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function addNodesToNetwork(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'element' | 'viewport'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  nodes: NewNode[],
  links: Array<[number, number]> = [],
): ApiResult<AddedElements> {
  if (nodes.length === 0) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_NODES', 'nodes must not be empty')
  }
  const isIndex = (i: number): boolean =>
    Number.isInteger(i) && i >= 0 && i < nodes.length
  const badLink = links.find(([from, to]) => !isIndex(from) || !isIndex(to))
  if (badLink !== undefined) {
    return failure(
      'RECIPE_BAD_LINK',
      `link [${badLink.join(', ')}] does not name two of the new nodes`,
    )
  }

  // Place the new nodes in a row below everything that is already there.
  const existing = apis.viewport.getNodePositions(networkId)
  if (!existing.success) return existing
  // A loop, not Math.min(...xs): see Pitfalls.
  let left = 0
  let bottom = 0
  let first = true
  for (const [x, y] of Object.values(existing.data.positions)) {
    left = first ? x : Math.min(left, x)
    bottom = first ? y : Math.max(bottom, y)
    first = false
  }

  const created = apis.element.createNodes(
    networkId,
    nodes.map((node, index) => ({
      position: [left + index * SPACING, bottom + SPACING],
      attributes: { ...node.attributes, name: node.name },
    })),
    { autoSelect: false },
  )
  if (!created.success) return created
  const nodeIds = created.data.nodes.map((n) => n.nodeId)
  if (links.length === 0) {
    return { success: true, data: { nodeIds, edgeIds: [] } }
  }

  const connected = apis.element.createEdges(
    networkId,
    links.map(([from, to]) => ({
      sourceNodeId: nodeIds[from],
      targetNodeId: nodeIds[to],
    })),
    { autoSelect: false },
  )
  // The nodes stay if this fails; see Pitfalls.
  if (!connected.success) return connected

  return {
    success: true,
    data: { nodeIds, edgeIds: connected.data.edges.map((e) => e.edgeId) },
  }
}
````

## Delete the selected nodes and edges

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/elements/delete-selected.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Delete the selected nodes and edges
 * @aliases delete selection, remove selected, delete selected nodes, remove
 *   nodes, delete edges, clear selected elements
 * @apis selection.getSelection, element.deleteNodes, element.deleteEdges
 * @related elements/add-edges-between-selected,
 *   selection/select-by-attribute, network/subnetwork-from-selection
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * An app deletes what the user selected, from code: a menu action, a button
 * in a panel, or as one step of a larger edit.
 *
 * The user can also choose Edit ▸ Delete Selected Nodes (or Edges), and on
 * 1.1.1 press Delete or Backspace on the canvas. This recipe does the same
 * from code, on both releases.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - Something in `networkId` is selected.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Deletes the selected nodes, every edge that touches them, and the
 *   selected edges.
 * - Records **one undo entry for the nodes and one for the edges** that
 *   remain to delete after them: the user undoes twice to restore a mixed
 *   selection.
 * - What Edit ▸ Undo restores differs by release. On 1.1.1 the nodes come
 *   back where they were. On 1.1.0 they come back without their views:
 *   `viewport.getNodePositions` lists them as missing, and the canvas draws
 *   them at (0, 0). 1.1.0's `deleteNodes` also reports every deleted node at
 *   `[0, 0]`. Both are fixed in 1.1.1 (host #857); both were seen by pressing
 *   Edit ▸ Undo on a host of each release.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Delete the nodes first.** Deleting a node deletes its edges, so the
 *   recipe then deletes only the selected edges that are still there.
 *   Deleting those edges first would work too, but leaves one more undo
 *   entry for edges the node deletion would have removed anyway.
 * - **Use the batch calls.** `deleteNodes` and `deleteEdges` each take every
 *   id at once and record one undo entry. A loop records one per element.
 * - **If the edges fail, the nodes stay deleted.** The recipe returns the
 *   failure; one undo restores the nodes.
 * - The two calls report ids that no longer exist in `missing` instead of
 *   failing, and fail only when none exists.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't delete nodes one at a time.
 * - Don't delete the selection of a network other than the one you mean:
 *   pass the current network's id, from `workspace.getCurrentNetworkId`.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface Deleted {
  nodeIds: IdType[]
  /** Every edge deleted: the selected ones and those of deleted nodes. */
  edgeIds: IdType[]
}

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function deleteSelected(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'selection' | 'element'>,
  networkId: IdType,
): ApiResult<Deleted> {
  const selection = apis.selection.getSelection(networkId)
  if (!selection.success) return selection
  const { selectedNodes, selectedEdges } = selection.data
  if (selectedNodes.length === 0 && selectedEdges.length === 0) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NOTHING_SELECTED', 'nothing is selected')
  }

  const deleted: Deleted = { nodeIds: [], edgeIds: [] }
  if (selectedNodes.length > 0) {
    const nodes = apis.element.deleteNodes(networkId, selectedNodes)
    if (!nodes.success) return nodes
    deleted.nodeIds = nodes.data.deletedNodes.map((n) => n.id)
    deleted.edgeIds = nodes.data.deletedEdges.map((e) => e.id)
  }

  const gone = new Set(deleted.edgeIds)
  const remaining = selectedEdges.filter((id) => !gone.has(id))
  if (remaining.length > 0) {
    const edges = apis.element.deleteEdges(networkId, remaining)
    if (!edges.success) return edges
    // concat, not push(...ids): a spread throws on a large selection.
    deleted.edgeIds = deleted.edgeIds.concat(
      edges.data.deletedEdges.map((e) => e.id),
    )
  }

  return { success: true, data: deleted }
}
````

## Follow the current network, and read it only when it is ready

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/events/follow-current-network.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Follow the current network, and read it only when it is ready
 * @aliases current network changed, network switched, on network change,
 *   react to network switch, wait for network to load, network not loaded,
 *   APP1 after switching, refresh when the user opens another network
 * @apis workspace.getCurrentNetworkId
 * @related elements/add-nodes-to-network, style/color-nodes-by-numeric-column
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The app shows or computes something about the network on screen and must
 * keep up when the user switches to another one.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The API is ready. Inside an app it always is. On a plain page, wait for
 *   `await window.CyWebApi.whenReady()` first.
 * - `read` returns `false` when it could not read the network yet, and `true`
 *   when it could. A failed read is how the recipe learns that the data has
 *   not arrived.
 * - `onNone`, if given, clears whatever the app shows about a network.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Adds two listeners on `window`: `network:switched` and `network:loaded`.
 *   `stop()` removes both.
 * - Calls `read` once at the start if a network is current, once for every
 *   switch, and once more when the data of a network it could not read
 *   arrives.
 * - Calls `onNone` at the start if no network is current, and whenever the
 *   last network is closed.
 * - Changes nothing in the host.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Switching is not loading.** After a page reload the workspace holds
 *   only summaries. A network's tables load the first time it becomes
 *   current, and `network:switched` fires before they arrive: a read made
 *   then fails with `APP1`. Read again on `network:loaded`.
 * - **Ignore events for other networks.** `network:loaded` also fires for
 *   networks that are not on screen. The recipe reads again only for the
 *   network it is waiting for.
 * - **Discard what arrives after a switch.** Each switch replaces the network
 *   being waited for, so a late `network:loaded` for the previous one is
 *   ignored. If `read` starts asynchronous work, check on completion that the
 *   network is still current before using the result.
 * - **Unsubscribe.** Call `stop()` in `unmount()`, or in the cleanup of a
 *   React effect. A listener that outlives its app keeps running after the
 *   app is disabled.
 * - **No network is a state too.** When the last network is closed, the
 *   host fires `network:switched` with an empty `networkId`. There is nothing
 *   to read, and what the app shows describes a network that is gone: the
 *   recipe calls `onNone` so that the app can clear it. At the start,
 *   `getCurrentNetworkId` fails when no network is open; that is the same
 *   state, not an error.
 * - Do not use a timer to wait for a load. There is no safe duration.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't read a network on `network:switched` and assume the read worked.
 * - Don't poll `getCurrentNetworkId`.
 * - Don't wait for the app's own panel or dialog inside `mount()`: the host
 *   shows them only after `mount()` returns.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. In an app, start it in
 * `mount()` and stop it in `unmount()`: see `wiring/from-mount.ts`. In a
 * component, the `useCyWebEvent` hook from `cyweb/EventBus` subscribes and
 * unsubscribes for you: see `wiring/from-panel.tsx`.
 */
import type { ApiResult, CyWebApiType, IdType } from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface FollowedNetwork {
  /** Removes both listeners. Safe to call more than once. */
  stop: () => void
}

export function followCurrentNetwork(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'workspace'>,
  read: (networkId: IdType) => boolean,
  onNone: () => void = () => {},
): ApiResult<FollowedNetwork> {
  // The network whose data had not arrived when `read` was last called.
  let waitingFor: IdType | null = null

  const deliver = (networkId: IdType): void => {
    waitingFor = read(networkId) ? null : networkId
  }

  const onSwitched = (event: WindowEventMap['network:switched']): void => {
    const { networkId } = event.detail
    if (networkId === '') {
      // The last network was closed: nothing is current.
      waitingFor = null
      onNone()
      return
    }
    deliver(networkId)
  }

  const onLoaded = (event: WindowEventMap['network:loaded']): void => {
    if (event.detail.networkId === waitingFor) deliver(event.detail.networkId)
  }

  window.addEventListener('network:switched', onSwitched)
  window.addEventListener('network:loaded', onLoaded)

  // 1. The network that is already on screen, if any.
  const current = apis.workspace.getCurrentNetworkId()
  if (current.success) deliver(current.data.networkId)
  else onNone()

  return {
    success: true,
    data: {
      stop: () => {
        window.removeEventListener('network:switched', onSwitched)
        window.removeEventListener('network:loaded', onLoaded)
      },
    },
  }
}
````

## Run a layout and wait for it to finish

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/layout/run-layout-and-wait.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Run a layout and wait for it to finish
 * @aliases apply layout, run layout, arrange nodes, layout network, wait for
 *   layout, force-directed layout, grid layout, re-layout, after layout
 * @apis layout.getAvailableLayouts, workspace.getCurrentNetworkId,
 *   layout.applyLayout
 * @related network/create-network-from-table,
 *   network/subnetwork-from-selection, events/follow-current-network
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * An app lays out a network and does something once the nodes have moved:
 * after building a network, after adding nodes, or as one step of an
 * analysis.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 * - `algorithmName`, if given, is one of `getAvailableLayouts()`'s
 *   `algorithmName`s. An app's own algorithm is named `<appId>::<id>`.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Moves the network's nodes, and records **one** undo entry.
 * - Fires `layout:started`, then `layout:completed` on success only.
 * - Fits the network's view when it is the current one, unless
 *   `fit: false`.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Await the promise, not the event.** `applyLayout` resolves once the
 *   nodes have moved, after `layout:completed`. It never rejects: a failure
 *   resolves to `success: false`, and no `layout:completed` follows it. Code
 *   that waits for the event waits forever on a failure.
 * - **Ignore events for other networks.** If you do listen to `layout:*`,
 *   compare `networkId`: another app, or the user, can lay out another
 *   network at the same time.
 * - **Discard what arrives after a switch.** The user can switch networks
 *   while a layout runs. `stillCurrent` says whether the network is still on
 *   screen; if not, do not move the user's view to it.
 * - **No network at all.** If the user closes the last network meanwhile,
 *   `stillCurrent` is false too.
 * - **The fit is the laid-out network's own.** On 1.1.0 and 1.1.1,
 *   `applyLayout` fits the canvas of `networkId` itself; a network with no
 *   canvas is laid out and not fitted, and the host logs a warning. The
 *   recipe asks for a fit only when the network is current, so that laying
 *   out a network in the background never moves a view.
 * - **Unsubscribe.** This recipe listens to nothing; if you add a listener,
 *   remove it when done.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't wait with a timer: layouts take from milliseconds to minutes.
 * - Don't write positions yourself to "lay out" a network the host can lay
 *   out.
 * - Don't guess algorithm names: read them from `getAvailableLayouts`.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface LayoutOptions {
  /** Defaults to the host's preferred layout. */
  algorithmName?: string
  /** Fit the view afterwards. Defaults to true when the network is current. */
  fit?: boolean
}

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export async function runLayoutAndWait(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'layout' | 'workspace'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  options: LayoutOptions = {},
): Promise<ApiResult<{ stillCurrent: boolean }>> {
  const { algorithmName } = options
  if (algorithmName !== undefined) {
    const available = apis.layout.getAvailableLayouts()
    if (!available.success) return available
    const names = available.data.layouts.map((l) => l.algorithmName)
    if (!names.includes(algorithmName)) {
      return failure(
        'RECIPE_UNKNOWN_LAYOUT',
        `no layout named ${algorithmName}; available: ${names.join(', ')}`,
      )
    }
  }

  const isCurrent = (): boolean => {
    const current = apis.workspace.getCurrentNetworkId()
    return current.success && current.data.networkId === networkId
  }

  const laidOut = await apis.layout.applyLayout(networkId, {
    algorithmName,
    fitAfterLayout: options.fit ?? isCurrent(),
  })
  if (!laidOut.success) return laidOut
  return { success: true, data: { stillCurrent: isCurrent() } }
}
````

## Create a network from a table of edges

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/network/create-network-from-table.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Create a network from a table of edges
 * @aliases import network from table, network from rows, edge list with
 *   attributes, build a network from data, network from a spreadsheet,
 *   source target table, interaction table
 * @apis network.createNetworkFromEdgeList, table.createColumn,
 *   table.editRows, network.deleteNetwork
 * @related network/subnetwork-from-selection, data/join-table-by-key,
 *   layout/run-layout-and-wait
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user has rows that each describe one edge, a source and a target plus
 * other values such as an interaction type or a weight, and asks for a
 * network from them: Cytoscape's "Import Network From Table".
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - Every row has a non-empty `source` and `target` value (the names of the
 *   two columns are arguments). Nodes are identified by these values.
 * - Every other column holds one type throughout: text, numbers or booleans.
 *   A row may leave a column out.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Adds a network to the workspace and makes it current (`network:created`,
 *   then `network:switched`). Its nodes get a `name` column holding the
 *   source and target values, shown as their labels.
 * - Creates one edge column per other column, and writes every edge's row in
 *   one batch: **one** undo entry on the new network. Creating a column
 *   records none.
 * - If writing a column fails, the recipe deletes the network it created:
 *   nothing is left behind.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **The host keeps nothing but the endpoints.** `createNetworkFromEdgeList`
 *   takes `[source, target, interaction?]`, and the edge table it creates is
 *   empty on both 1.1.0 and 1.1.1: the third element is dropped. The recipe
 *   writes every other column, `interaction` included, itself.
 * - **Edges are matched to rows by order.** The host creates the edges in the
 *   order of the edge list, and returns them in that order; the recipe pairs
 *   row `i` with edge `i`. Its case checks this on both releases.
 * - **The edges have no table rows, so `setValues` writes nothing.** On both
 *   1.1.0 and 1.1.1, `setValue` and `setValues` change only rows that
 *   exist, and report success either way; an edge-list network has a row
 *   for every node and none for its edges. `editRows` creates the rows. It
 *   also replaces a row whole, dropping values it is not given: use it only
 *   for rows written completely, as these new ones are.
 * - **One batch.** `editRows` validates every value first and writes all or
 *   nothing, with one undo entry.
 * - **A row that leaves a column out has no value in it**, not the column's
 *   default.
 * - **Column names.** `id`, `s`, `t`, `source` and `target` are refused, and
 *   so are two names that differ only by case: 1.1.0 would create two
 *   columns, and 1.1.1 refuses the second with `AC6`.
 * - **The new network is current, and on 1.1.0 the table browser and layout
 *   tools still act on the one shown before** until the user picks the new
 *   one in the workspace. 1.1.1 fixes this (host #927). Calls that take a
 *   `networkId` are not affected on either.
 * - The nodes have no layout yet. Run one: `layout/run-layout-and-wait`.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't pass edge attributes as the third element of the edge list and
 *   expect to find them in the edge table.
 * - Don't create one network per row, or add edges one by one to an empty
 *   network.
 * - Don't guess edge ids (`e0`, `e1`, …): use the ones the host returns.
 * - Don't write edge values with `setValues` after `createNetworkFromEdgeList`:
 *   it reports success and writes nothing.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
  ValueTypeName,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export type Cell = string | number | boolean

export interface EdgeTableColumns {
  /** The column that names each edge's source node. */
  source: string
  /** The column that names each edge's target node. */
  target: string
}

export interface CreatedNetwork {
  networkId: IdType
  /** The edges' ids, in the order of the rows. */
  edgeIds: IdType[]
  /** The edge columns created, with their types. */
  columns: Record<string, ValueTypeName>
}

const RESERVED = ['id', 's', 't', 'source', 'target']

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

const defaultFor = (type: ValueTypeName): Cell =>
  type === 'string' ? '' : type === 'boolean' ? false : 0

export function createNetworkFromTable(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'network' | 'table'>,
  name: string,
  rows: Array<Record<string, Cell | undefined>>,
  columns: EdgeTableColumns,
): ApiResult<CreatedNetwork> {
  if (rows.length === 0) return failure('RECIPE_NO_ROWS', 'rows is empty')

  // Check everything before creating anything.
  const edgeList: Array<[string, string]> = []
  const types = new Map<string, ValueTypeName>()
  for (const [index, row] of rows.entries()) {
    const source = row[columns.source]
    const target = row[columns.target]
    if (source === undefined || source === '' || target === undefined ||
        target === '') {
      return failure(
        'RECIPE_MISSING_ENDPOINT',
        `row ${index} has no ${columns.source} or no ${columns.target}`,
      )
    }
    edgeList.push([String(source), String(target)])

    for (const [column, value] of Object.entries(row)) {
      if (column === columns.source || column === columns.target) continue
      if (value === undefined) continue
      const type: ValueTypeName =
        typeof value === 'boolean'
          ? 'boolean'
          : typeof value === 'number'
            ? Number.isInteger(value) ? 'long' : 'double'
            : 'string'
      const known = types.get(column)
      if (known === undefined || (known === 'long' && type === 'double')) {
        types.set(column, type)
      } else if (known !== type && !(known === 'double' && type === 'long')) {
        return failure(
          'RECIPE_MIXED_TYPES',
          `column ${column} holds both ${known} and ${type} values`,
        )
      }
    }
  }
  const lowered = new Set<string>()
  for (const column of types.keys()) {
    const key = column.toLowerCase()
    if (RESERVED.includes(key) || lowered.has(key)) {
      return failure(
        'RECIPE_COLUMN_NAME',
        `${column} is reserved, or differs from another column only by case`,
      )
    }
    lowered.add(key)
  }

  const created = apis.network.createNetworkFromEdgeList({ name, edgeList })
  if (!created.success) return created
  const { networkId } = created.data
  const edgeIds = created.data.cyNetwork.network.edges.map((e) => e.id)

  // From here on, a failure removes the network again.
  const undo = (result: ApiFailure): ApiFailure => {
    apis.network.deleteNetwork(networkId)
    return result
  }
  if (edgeIds.length !== rows.length) {
    return undo(
      failure(
        'RECIPE_EDGE_COUNT',
        `${rows.length} rows made ${edgeIds.length} edges`,
      ),
    )
  }

  for (const [column, type] of types) {
    const made = apis.table.createColumn(
      networkId,
      'edge',
      column,
      type,
      defaultFor(type),
    )
    if (!made.success) return undo(made)
  }
  // One row per edge, holding the row's own values: see Pitfalls.
  const edgeRows: Record<IdType, Record<string, Cell>> = {}
  rows.forEach((row, index) => {
    const values: Record<string, Cell> = {}
    for (const column of types.keys()) {
      const value = row[column]
      if (value !== undefined) values[column] = value
    }
    edgeRows[edgeIds[index]] = values
  })
  const written = apis.table.editRows(networkId, 'edge', edgeRows)
  if (!written.success) return undo(written)

  return {
    success: true,
    data: { networkId, edgeIds, columns: Object.fromEntries(types) },
  }
}
````

## Create a new network from the selected nodes

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/network/subnetwork-from-selection.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Create a new network from the selected nodes
 * @aliases subnetwork, extract selection, new network from selection,
 *   network from selected nodes, induced subgraph, sub-network, copy
 *   selection to a new network
 * @apis selection.getSelection, element.getEdges,
 *   network.createNetworkFromNodeList, visualStyle.getVisualStyle,
 *   visualStyle.applyVisualStyle, network.deleteNetwork
 * @related network/create-network-from-table,
 *   selection/select-neighbors, selection/select-by-attribute
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user has selected part of a network and wants it as a network of its
 * own: Cytoscape's "New Network From Selection".
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - At least one node of `networkId` is selected.
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Adds a network to the workspace and makes it current. Its nodes and edges
 *   keep their ids, columns, values and positions.
 * - `edges: 'induced'` (the default) takes every edge between two selected
 *   nodes. `edges: 'selected'` takes only the selected edges among them.
 * - With `copyStyle` (the default), the new network gets a copy of the source
 *   network's active style: one undo entry on the new network. Without it, it
 *   has the host's default style and a label mapping from `name`.
 * - If copying the style fails, the recipe deletes the network it created.
 * - The source network is not changed.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Style is not copied by the host.** `createNetworkFromNodeList` gives
 *   the new network a default style on both 1.1.0 and 1.1.1. The recipe
 *   copies it with `getVisualStyle` and `applyVisualStyle`.
 * - **Bypasses are not copied.** `applyVisualStyle` drops them, although the
 *   ids would match. A node highlighted in the source is not highlighted in
 *   the subnetwork.
 * - **One call, not a loop.** `createNetworkFromNodeList` copies everything
 *   in one step, and fails without creating anything if an id is unknown.
 *   The other way, `export.exportToCx2` and `createNetworkFromCx2`, takes
 *   two calls and a whole CX2 document to make the same network.
 * - **`'selected'` edges must connect selected nodes**, or the host refuses
 *   the call (`APP9`). The recipe leaves out a selected edge with an
 *   unselected end.
 * - **The new network is current, and on 1.1.0 the table browser and layout
 *   tools still act on the one shown before** until the user picks the new
 *   one in the workspace. 1.1.1 fixes this (host #927).
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't rebuild the subnetwork with `createNetworkFromEdgeList`: it loses
 *   every column, the ids and the positions.
 * - Don't copy the style by setting the same defaults and mappings again.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface SubnetworkOptions {
  /** Defaults to "Subnetwork of <source name>". */
  name?: string
  /** Which edges to take. Defaults to every edge between selected nodes. */
  edges?: 'induced' | 'selected'
  /** Copy the source network's active style. Defaults to true. */
  copyStyle?: boolean
}

export interface Subnetwork {
  networkId: IdType
  nodeCount: number
  edgeCount: number
}

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function subnetworkFromSelection(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'selection' | 'element' | 'network' | 'visualStyle'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  options: SubnetworkOptions = {},
): ApiResult<Subnetwork> {
  const selection = apis.selection.getSelection(networkId)
  if (!selection.success) return selection
  const { selectedNodes, selectedEdges } = selection.data
  if (selectedNodes.length === 0) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NOTHING_SELECTED', 'no node is selected')
  }

  let edgeIds: IdType[] | 'all' = 'all'
  if (options.edges === 'selected') {
    const chosen = new Set(selectedNodes)
    const edges = apis.element.getEdges(networkId, selectedEdges)
    if (!edges.success) return edges
    edgeIds = edges.data.edges
      .filter((e) => chosen.has(e.sourceId) && chosen.has(e.targetId))
      .map((e) => e.id)
  }

  // Read the style first, so that a failure here creates nothing.
  const copyStyle = options.copyStyle ?? true
  const style = copyStyle ? apis.visualStyle.getVisualStyle(networkId) : null
  if (style !== null && !style.success) return style

  const created = apis.network.createNetworkFromNodeList(
    networkId,
    selectedNodes,
    edgeIds,
    { name: options.name },
  )
  if (!created.success) return created
  const subnetwork = created.data.cyNetwork.network

  if (style !== null) {
    const copied = apis.visualStyle.applyVisualStyle(
      subnetwork.id,
      style.data.visualStyle,
      { name: 'Copied style' },
    )
    if (!copied.success) {
      apis.network.deleteNetwork(subnetwork.id)
      return copied
    }
  }

  return {
    success: true,
    data: {
      networkId: subnetwork.id,
      nodeCount: subnetwork.nodes.length,
      edgeCount: subnetwork.edges.length,
    },
  }
}
````

## Select nodes or edges by a column's value

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/selection/select-by-attribute.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Select nodes or edges by a column's value
 * @aliases select by attribute, select where, find nodes with, select
 *   matching nodes, filter selection, select by value, select by type,
 *   query nodes
 * @apis table.getTable, selection.exclusiveSelect, selection.additiveSelect
 * @related selection/select-neighbors, network/subnetwork-from-selection,
 *   style/highlight-with-bypass
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user asks to select the nodes (or edges) whose value in a column meets
 * a condition: "select all kinases", "select edges with weight over 0.8".
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 * - `test` is a function of one value that returns `true` to select.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - `mode: 'replace'` (the default) makes the matches the whole selection.
 *   `'add'` adds them to it.
 * - Fires `selection:changed`. Records no undo entry.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Values keep their column's type.** In a `long` column, `5` is a
 *   number: `(v) => v === '5'` matches nothing. Compare with the type the
 *   column has.
 * - **Text is compared exactly.** `"Kinase"` is not `"kinase"`; lower-case
 *   both sides in `test` if that is what the user means.
 * - **Missing values never match.** `test` sees only elements that have a
 *   value; `missing` counts the others.
 * - **A list column** passes the whole list to `test`.
 * - **`test` must not throw.** If it does, the recipe stops before selecting
 *   anything and returns `RECIPE_TEST_THREW`.
 * - **On 1.1.0, changing the selection from code shows hidden elements again
 *   on the canvas.** See `style/hide-by-threshold`. 1.1.1 fixes this.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't read the values one `getValue` call at a time.
 * - Don't select by matching a node's label: labels come from a mapping, and
 *   may show another column than the one meant.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  AppTableType,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
  ValueType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface SelectOptions {
  /** Defaults to `'node'`. */
  tableType?: AppTableType
  /** Replace the selection, or add to it. Defaults to `'replace'`. */
  mode?: 'replace' | 'add'
}

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function selectByAttribute(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'table' | 'selection'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  column: string,
  test: (value: ValueType) => boolean,
  options: SelectOptions = {},
): ApiResult<{ selectedIds: IdType[]; missing: number }> {
  const tableType = options.tableType ?? 'node'
  const table = apis.table.getTable(networkId, tableType, { columns: [column] })
  if (!table.success) return table
  if (!table.data.columns.some((c) => c.name === column)) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_COLUMN', `no ${tableType} column ${column}`)
  }

  const matches: IdType[] = []
  let missing = 0
  for (const row of table.data.rows) {
    const value = row[column]
    if (value === undefined || value === null) {
      missing += 1
      continue
    }
    try {
      if (test(value)) matches.push(String(row.id))
    } catch (cause) {
      return failure(
        'RECIPE_TEST_THREW',
        `test threw on ${String(row.id)}: ${String(cause)}`,
      )
    }
  }

  const nodes = tableType === 'node' ? matches : []
  const edges = tableType === 'edge' ? matches : []
  const selected =
    options.mode === 'add'
      ? apis.selection.additiveSelect(networkId, nodes, edges)
      : apis.selection.exclusiveSelect(networkId, nodes, edges)
  if (!selected.success) return selected
  return { success: true, data: { selectedIds: matches, missing } }
}
````

## Select the neighbors of the selected nodes

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/selection/select-neighbors.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Select the neighbors of the selected nodes
 * @aliases first neighbors, select neighbors, expand selection, select
 *   adjacent nodes, second neighbors, neighborhood, n hops, k-hop
 *   neighborhood, grow selection
 * @apis selection.getSelection, element.getEdges, selection.additiveSelect
 * @related selection/select-by-attribute, network/subnetwork-from-selection,
 *   elements/add-edges-between-selected
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user asks to select what is connected to the current selection:
 * Cytoscape's "First Neighbors of Selected Nodes", or neighbors up to a
 * number of hops away.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - At least one node of `networkId` is selected.
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Adds every node within `hops` edges of a selected node to the selection.
 *   The nodes and edges selected before stay selected.
 * - Fires `selection:changed`. Records no undo entry.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Hops count from the starting selection.** `hops: 2` selects the first
 *   neighbors and their neighbors. Each round starts only from the nodes the
 *   last round added.
 * - **Direction.** `'any'` (the default) follows edges both ways.
 *   `'outgoing'` follows an edge from its source to its target only, and
 *   `'incoming'` the other way.
 * - **Read the edges once.** One `getEdges` call returns every edge with its
 *   ends. One `getConnectedNodes` call per node per hop does the same work a
 *   node at a time.
 * - **On 1.1.0, changing the selection from code shows hidden elements again
 *   on the canvas.** See `style/hide-by-threshold`. 1.1.1 fixes this.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't replace the selection with the neighbors alone, unless the user
 *   asks for that: `exclusiveSelect` drops the nodes they started from.
 * - Don't select the edges between the neighbors unless asked: the host's
 *   own command selects nodes only.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface NeighborOptions {
  /** How many edges away. Defaults to 1. */
  hops?: number
  /** Which way to follow edges. Defaults to `'any'`. */
  direction?: 'any' | 'outgoing' | 'incoming'
}

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function selectNeighbors(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'selection' | 'element'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  options: NeighborOptions = {},
): ApiResult<{ addedNodeIds: IdType[] }> {
  const hops = options.hops ?? 1
  const direction = options.direction ?? 'any'
  if (!Number.isInteger(hops) || hops < 1) {
    return failure('RECIPE_BAD_HOPS', 'hops must be a whole number, 1 or more')
  }

  const selection = apis.selection.getSelection(networkId)
  if (!selection.success) return selection
  const start = selection.data.selectedNodes
  if (start.length === 0) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NOTHING_SELECTED', 'no node is selected')
  }

  const edges = apis.element.getEdges(networkId)
  if (!edges.success) return edges
  const next = new Map<IdType, IdType[]>()
  const link = (from: IdType, to: IdType): void => {
    const list = next.get(from)
    if (list === undefined) next.set(from, [to])
    else list.push(to)
  }
  for (const edge of edges.data.edges) {
    if (direction !== 'incoming') link(edge.sourceId, edge.targetId)
    if (direction !== 'outgoing') link(edge.targetId, edge.sourceId)
  }

  const reached = new Set<IdType>(start)
  const added: IdType[] = []
  let frontier = start
  for (let hop = 0; hop < hops && frontier.length > 0; hop += 1) {
    const found: IdType[] = []
    for (const node of frontier) {
      for (const neighbor of next.get(node) ?? []) {
        if (!reached.has(neighbor)) {
          reached.add(neighbor)
          found.push(neighbor)
        }
      }
    }
    for (const id of found) added.push(id)
    frontier = found
  }

  if (added.length > 0) {
    const selected = apis.selection.additiveSelect(networkId, added, [])
    if (!selected.success) return selected
  }
  return { success: true, data: { addedNodeIds: added } }
}
````

## Color nodes by category

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/style/color-by-category.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Color nodes by category
 * @aliases color by type, color by group, color by class, categorical
 *   colors, discrete color mapping, one color per value, color by label,
 *   legend colors
 * @apis table.getTable, visualStyle.createDiscreteMapping
 * @related style/color-nodes-by-numeric-column, style/label-from-column,
 *   style/set-style-defaults
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user asks for each kind of node to have its own color: by a column of
 * names, types or group numbers, not by a quantity.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 * - `column` is a node column of type `string`, `integer` or `long`.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Replaces any mapping on the node fill color (`nodeBackgroundColor`) with
 *   a discrete mapping: one palette color per distinct value, in sorted
 *   order. Mappings record no undo entry.
 * - Changes no table data and no bypass.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **More categories than colors.** The palette has eight colors, chosen to
 *   stay distinct for color-blind readers (Okabe and Ito). Values past the
````
