````typescript
 *   eighth keep the default color and are listed in `uncolored`. Pass a
 *   longer palette, or color only what matters.
 * - **Boolean columns never match.** The host keys a discrete mapping by the
 *   text of each key, and converts it back to a number for `integer`, `long`
 *   and `double` columns only. `true` stays the string `"true"` and matches
 *   no boolean value. The recipe refuses boolean columns.
 * - **Values are compared exactly.** `"Kinase"` and `"kinase"` are two
 *   categories. Normalize the column first if they are the same thing.
 * - **List columns** are matched by their first item only. The recipe
 *   refuses them.
 * - **Missing values**, and values past the palette, show the mapping's
 *   fallback: the default color as it was when the mapping was made. A later
 *   default does not reach them (`style/set-style-defaults`).
 * - **Order is sorted, not by frequency,** so the same values get the same
 *   colors every time the recipe runs.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't use a continuous mapping for categories: group 3 is not "between"
 *   groups 2 and 4.
 * - Don't set a fill bypass on every node: it does not follow the data.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

/** A color as the host stores it: `#rrggbb`. */
export type HexColor = `#${string}`

export interface CategoryColors {
  /** The color of each value, by the value's text. */
  colors: Record<string, HexColor>
  /** Values that got no color: they keep the default. */
  uncolored: string[]
}

/** Okabe and Ito's palette, distinct for the common forms of color blindness. */
export const CATEGORY_PALETTE: HexColor[] = [
  '#e69f00', '#56b4e9', '#009e73', '#f0e442',
  '#0072b2', '#d55e00', '#cc79a7', '#000000',
]

const ALLOWED_TYPES = ['string', 'integer', 'long']

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function colorByCategory(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'table' | 'visualStyle'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  column: string,
  palette: HexColor[] = CATEGORY_PALETTE,
): ApiResult<CategoryColors> {
  const table = apis.table.getTable(networkId, 'node', { columns: [column] })
  if (!table.success) return table
  const info = table.data.columns.find((c) => c.name === column)
  if (info === undefined) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_COLUMN', `no node column named ${column}`)
  }
  if (!ALLOWED_TYPES.includes(info.type)) {
    return failure(
      'RECIPE_COLUMN_TYPE',
      `${column} is a ${info.type} column; use string, integer or long`,
    )
  }

  const distinct = new Set<string | number>()
  for (const row of table.data.rows) {
    const value = row[column]
    if (typeof value === 'string' ? value !== '' : typeof value === 'number') {
      distinct.add(value as string | number)
    }
  }
  if (distinct.size === 0) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_VALUES', `${column} has no value`)
  }
  const values = [...distinct].sort((a, b) =>
    typeof a === 'number' && typeof b === 'number'
      ? a - b
      : String(a).localeCompare(String(b)),
  )

  const colors: Record<string, HexColor> = {}
  const uncolored: string[] = []
  values.forEach((value, index) => {
    if (index < palette.length) colors[String(value)] = palette[index]
    else uncolored.push(String(value))
  })

  const mapped = apis.visualStyle.createDiscreteMapping(
    networkId,
    'nodeBackgroundColor',
    column,
    info.type,
    colors,
  )
  if (!mapped.success) return mapped
  return { success: true, data: { colors, uncolored } }
}
````

## Color nodes by a numeric column

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/style/color-nodes-by-numeric-column.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Color nodes by a numeric column
 * @aliases color by score, color by value, heat map, heatmap, gradient,
 *   color scale, continuous color mapping, color nodes from blue to red,
 *   expression coloring
 * @apis table.getTable, visualStyle.createContinuousMapping
 * @related elements/add-nodes-to-network, events/follow-current-network
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user asks to color nodes along a gradient by a number in the node
 * table: "color the nodes from blue to red by their `score` column".
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 * - `column` is a node column of type `double`, `long` or `integer`.
 * - At least two nodes have different, finite values in it.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Replaces any mapping on the node fill color (`nodeBackgroundColor`) of
 *   the network's active style with a continuous mapping.
 * - Marks the network as modified.
 * - Changes no table data and no bypass. A node with a color bypass keeps its
 *   bypass color: a bypass wins over a mapping.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Missing values.** A node with no value in the column is not colored by
 *   the mapping. It keeps the style's default color. The recipe reports how
 *   many nodes that is in `unmappedCount`.
 * - **Non-numeric values.** A `string` column cannot drive a continuous
 *   mapping, even when its cells look like numbers. The recipe fails with
 *   `RECIPE_COLUMN_NOT_NUMERIC` before it changes anything. Values that are
 *   not finite (`NaN`, `Infinity`) are left out of the range.
 * - **An empty column.** With no finite value there is no range, and the
 *   recipe fails with `RECIPE_NO_VALUES`.
 * - **All values equal.** A range of zero width has no gradient, and the
 *   recipe fails with `RECIPE_SINGLE_VALUE`. Set one default color instead
 *   (`visualStyle.setDefault`).
 * - **`attributeType` must be the column's own type.** Read it from the
 *   table. Passing `'long'` for a `double` column fails with `MI2`.
 * - **Find the range with a loop.** `Math.min(...values)` passes one argument
 *   per node, and throws a `RangeError` past about 120,000 of them. The host
 *   does not stop a network of that size from loading.
 * - **Pass the two control points yourself.** Without them the host uses its
 *   own three-color scheme, and takes the first and last entries of
 *   `attributeValues` as the range, whatever their order.
 * - Visual property names are camelCase strings such as
 *   `'nodeBackgroundColor'`, checked by the `VisualPropertyName` type.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't set a bypass on every node to color a network. Bypasses are for
 *   exceptions, and they hide every later mapping.
 * - Don't invent a visual property name such as `'NODE_FILL_COLOR'`.
 * - Don't hard-code the range. Read the values first.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

/** A color as the host stores it: `#rrggbb`. */
export type HexColor = `#${string}`

export interface NodeColorScale {
  /** Color of the lowest value. Defaults to blue. */
  low?: HexColor
  /** Color of the highest value. Defaults to red. */
  high?: HexColor
}

export interface ColoredNodes {
  min: number
  max: number
  /** Nodes with a finite value: the mapping colors these. */
  mappedCount: number
  /** Nodes without one: these keep the default color. */
  unmappedCount: number
}

const NUMERIC_TYPES = ['double', 'long', 'integer']

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function colorNodesByNumericColumn(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'table' | 'visualStyle'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  column: string,
  scale: NodeColorScale = {},
): ApiResult<ColoredNodes> {
  const table = apis.table.getTable(networkId, 'node', { columns: [column] })
  if (!table.success) return table

  const info = table.data.columns.find((c) => c.name === column)
  if (info === undefined) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_COLUMN', `no node column named "${column}"`)
  }
  if (!NUMERIC_TYPES.includes(info.type)) {
    return failure(
      'RECIPE_COLUMN_NOT_NUMERIC',
      `"${column}" is of type ${info.type}; a gradient needs a number`,
    )
  }

  // A loop, not Math.min(...values): see Pitfalls.
  let min = Infinity
  let max = -Infinity
  let mappedCount = 0
  for (const row of table.data.rows) {
    const value = row[column]
    if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)) continue
    mappedCount += 1
    min = Math.min(min, value)
    max = Math.max(max, value)
  }
  if (mappedCount === 0) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_VALUES', `"${column}" has no numeric value`)
  }
  if (min === max) {
    return failure(
      'RECIPE_SINGLE_VALUE',
      `every value of "${column}" is ${min}; there is nothing to grade`,
    )
  }

  const low: HexColor = scale.low ?? '#2166ac'
  const high: HexColor = scale.high ?? '#b2182b'
  const mapped = apis.visualStyle.createContinuousMapping(
    networkId,
    'nodeBackgroundColor',
    {
      vpType: 'color',
      attribute: column,
      attributeType: info.type,
      attributeValues: [min, max],
      controlPoints: [
        { value: min, vpValue: low },
        { value: max, vpValue: high },
      ],
      ltMinVpValue: low,
      gtMaxVpValue: high,
    },
  )
  if (!mapped.success) return mapped

  return {
    success: true,
    data: {
      min,
      max,
      mappedCount,
      unmappedCount: table.data.rows.length - mappedCount,
    },
  }
}
````

## Emphasize nodes past a threshold

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/style/emphasize-by-threshold.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Emphasize nodes past a threshold
 * @aliases highlight nodes above a value, mark significant nodes, threshold
 *   border, emphasize high scores, nodes over cutoff, outline nodes above a
 *   threshold, step mapping
 * @apis table.getTable, visualStyle.getDefault,
 *   visualStyle.createContinuousMapping, visualStyle.deleteMapping
 * @related style/hide-by-threshold, style/highlight-with-bypass,
 *   style/color-nodes-by-numeric-column
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user asks for nodes at or above a value to stand out, "outline the
 * genes with fold change of at least 2", while the rest stay as they are.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 * - `column` is a node column of type `double`, `long` or `integer`.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Replaces any mapping on the node border color and border width with a
 *   step: below the threshold, the current default; at or above it, the
 *   emphasis. Mappings record no undo entry.
 * - If the second mapping fails, the recipe deletes the first again.
 * - Changes no table data and no bypass.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **A mapping, not a bypass.** The emphasis follows the data: when a value
 *   changes, so does its node. A bypass would mark the nodes that passed
 *   once, and stay.
 * - **One control point makes a step.** The host's continuous mapping uses
 *   `ltMinVpValue` below the point, the point's own value at it, and
 *   `gtMaxVpValue` above it. A value exactly at the threshold is emphasized.
 * - **Missing values** get the mapping's fallback, the default border when
 *   the mapping was made: a node with no value is not emphasized.
 * - **Non-numeric values.** A text column is refused, even when it holds
 *   digits. Convert it first (`data/read-column-values-safely`).
 * - **An empty column** emphasizes nothing; **all values equal** emphasizes
 *   all or none. Both are reported by `emphasized`.
 * - **The low side is the default at the time of the call.** If the defaults
 *   change later, nodes below the threshold keep the old border. Run the
 *   recipe again.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't loop over the nodes and set a bypass on those that pass.
 * - Don't change the fill color to emphasize: it hides a color mapping.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

/** A color as the host stores it: `#rrggbb`. */
export type HexColor = `#${string}`

export interface EmphasisOptions {
  /** Border color at or above the threshold. Defaults to vermillion. */
  color?: HexColor
  /** Border width at or above the threshold. Defaults to 8. */
  width?: number
}

const NUMERIC_TYPES = ['double', 'long', 'integer']

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function emphasizeByThreshold(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'table' | 'visualStyle'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  column: string,
  threshold: number,
  options: EmphasisOptions = {},
): ApiResult<{ emphasized: number }> {
  if (!Number.isFinite(threshold)) {
    return failure('RECIPE_BAD_THRESHOLD', 'threshold must be a number')
  }
  const table = apis.table.getTable(networkId, 'node', { columns: [column] })
  if (!table.success) return table
  const info = table.data.columns.find((c) => c.name === column)
  if (info === undefined) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_COLUMN', `no node column named ${column}`)
  }
  if (!NUMERIC_TYPES.includes(info.type)) {
    return failure(
      'RECIPE_COLUMN_NOT_NUMERIC',
      `${column} is a ${info.type} column`,
    )
  }

  const baseColor = apis.visualStyle.getDefault(networkId, 'nodeBorderColor')
  if (!baseColor.success) return baseColor
  const baseWidth = apis.visualStyle.getDefault(networkId, 'nodeBorderWidth')
  if (!baseWidth.success) return baseWidth

  const step = (
    vpName: 'nodeBorderColor' | 'nodeBorderWidth',
    below: string | number,
    atOrAbove: string | number,
  ): ApiResult =>
    apis.visualStyle.createContinuousMapping(networkId, vpName, {
      vpType: vpName === 'nodeBorderColor' ? 'color' : 'number',
      attribute: column,
      attributeType: info.type,
      attributeValues: [threshold],
      controlPoints: [{ value: threshold, vpValue: atOrAbove }],
      ltMinVpValue: below,
      gtMaxVpValue: atOrAbove,
    })
  const colored = step(
    'nodeBorderColor',
    baseColor.data.value as string,
    options.color ?? '#d55e00',
  )
  if (!colored.success) return colored
  const widened = step(
    'nodeBorderWidth',
    baseWidth.data.value as number,
    options.width ?? 8,
  )
  if (!widened.success) {
    apis.visualStyle.deleteMapping(networkId, 'nodeBorderColor')
    return widened
  }

  let emphasized = 0
  for (const row of table.data.rows) {
    const value = row[column]
    if (typeof value === 'number' && value >= threshold) emphasized += 1
  }
  return { success: true, data: { emphasized } }
}
````

## Hide nodes below a threshold

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/style/hide-by-threshold.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Hide nodes below a threshold
 * @aliases filter nodes, hide nodes, hide low values, show only nodes above,
 *   remove from view, cutoff filter, hide edges of hidden nodes, show again
 * @apis table.getTable, element.getEdges, visualStyle.getBypasses,
 *   visualStyle.setBypass, visualStyle.deleteBypass
 * @related style/emphasize-by-threshold, selection/select-by-attribute,
 *   elements/delete-selected
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user asks to see only the nodes at or above a value, without deleting
 * the others: "hide everything with a score below 0.5".
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 * - `column` is a node column of type `double`, `long` or `integer`.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Sets a `nodeVisibility` bypass of `'none'` on every node below the
 *   threshold, and an `edgeVisibility` one on every edge that touches such a
 *   node, as the host's own Hide Selected does on 1.1.1.
 * - Leaves elements that were already hidden as they were, and returns
 *   `show()`, which shows again only what the recipe hid.
 * - Records **no** undo entry. Bypasses are saved with the network until
 *   removed.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Missing values.** A node with no value is kept by default; pass
 *   `hideMissing: true` to hide it too.
 * - **Non-numeric values.** A text column is refused.
 * - **An empty column** hides nothing, or everything with `hideMissing`.
 *   **All values equal** hides all or none.
 * - **Hiding is a bypass, so it does not follow the data.** A node whose
 *   value rises later stays hidden: call `show()` and run the recipe again.
 * - **The host can show the nodes again.** The FILTER tab, in its show mode,
 *   replaces every visibility bypass of the network on both releases, and
 *   on 1.1.1 Select ▸ Show All removes them all. Both undo the recipe's
 *   hiding.
 * - **On 1.1.0 a selection change can show hidden elements on the canvas**,
 *   while the style still says they are hidden. The host's renderer showed
 *   every element whenever the selection changed from outside the canvas,
 *   for example by the selection API. 1.1.1 fixes this (`0f8b7f42`). The
 *   case sees both behaviors.
 * - **Use one call per property.** `setBypass` takes every id at once. If
 *   the edges fail, the recipe shows the nodes again, so nothing is left
 *   half-hidden.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't delete the nodes to hide them: the user cannot get them back
 *   without undo.
 * - Don't hide nodes and leave their edges: a hidden node's edges would
 *   point at nothing.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface Hidden {
  nodeIds: IdType[]
  edgeIds: IdType[]
  /** Show again what this call hid, and nothing else. */
  show: () => ApiResult
}

const NUMERIC_TYPES = ['double', 'long', 'integer']

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function hideByThreshold(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'table' | 'element' | 'visualStyle'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  column: string,
  threshold: number,
  options: { hideMissing?: boolean } = {},
): ApiResult<Hidden> {
  if (!Number.isFinite(threshold)) {
    return failure('RECIPE_BAD_THRESHOLD', 'threshold must be a number')
  }
  const table = apis.table.getTable(networkId, 'node', { columns: [column] })
  if (!table.success) return table
  const info = table.data.columns.find((c) => c.name === column)
  if (info === undefined) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_COLUMN', `no node column named ${column}`)
  }
  if (!NUMERIC_TYPES.includes(info.type)) {
    return failure(
      'RECIPE_COLUMN_NOT_NUMERIC',
      `${column} is a ${info.type} column`,
    )
  }

  const hiddenNodes = apis.visualStyle.getBypasses(networkId, 'nodeVisibility')
  if (!hiddenNodes.success) return hiddenNodes
  const hiddenEdges = apis.visualStyle.getBypasses(networkId, 'edgeVisibility')
  if (!hiddenEdges.success) return hiddenEdges

  const below = new Set<IdType>()
  for (const row of table.data.rows) {
    const value = row[column]
    const fails =
      typeof value === 'number'
        ? value < threshold
        : options.hideMissing === true
    if (fails) below.add(String(row.id))
  }
  const nodeIds = [...below].filter((id) => !(id in hiddenNodes.data.bypasses))

  const edges = apis.element.getEdges(networkId)
  if (!edges.success) return edges
  const edgeIds = edges.data.edges
    .filter((e) => below.has(e.sourceId) || below.has(e.targetId))
    .map((e) => e.id)
    .filter((id) => !(id in hiddenEdges.data.bypasses))

  const show = (): ApiResult => {
    if (nodeIds.length > 0) {
      const shown = apis.visualStyle.deleteBypass(
        networkId,
        'nodeVisibility',
        nodeIds,
      )
      if (!shown.success) return shown
    }
    if (edgeIds.length > 0) {
      const shown = apis.visualStyle.deleteBypass(
        networkId,
        'edgeVisibility',
        edgeIds,
      )
      if (!shown.success) return shown
    }
    return { success: true, data: undefined }
  }

  if (nodeIds.length > 0) {
    const hid = apis.visualStyle.setBypass(
      networkId,
      'nodeVisibility',
      nodeIds,
      'none',
    )
    if (!hid.success) return hid
  }
  if (edgeIds.length > 0) {
    const hid = apis.visualStyle.setBypass(
      networkId,
      'edgeVisibility',
      edgeIds,
      'none',
    )
    if (!hid.success) {
      show()
      return hid
    }
  }
  return { success: true, data: { nodeIds, edgeIds, show } }
}
````

## Highlight some nodes, and remove the highlight later

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/style/highlight-with-bypass.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Highlight some nodes, and remove the highlight later
 * @aliases highlight nodes, mark nodes, emphasize these nodes, flag nodes,
 *   outline nodes, temporary highlight, bypass, override style for some
 *   nodes
 * @apis visualStyle.getBypasses, visualStyle.setBypasses,
 *   visualStyle.setBypass, visualStyle.deleteBypass
 * @related style/emphasize-by-threshold, style/set-style-defaults,
 *   selection/select-by-attribute
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * An app marks particular nodes for the user to see, such as the hits of a
 * search or the result of an analysis, and takes the mark away again.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - `nodeIds` name nodes of `networkId`.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Sets a border color and width bypass on those nodes. Their fill, label
 *   and any mapping stay as they are.
 * - Returns `clear()`, which puts back exactly the bypasses those nodes had
 *   before: none, or the earlier values.
 * - Records **no** undo entry. Edit ▸ Undo does not remove a highlight; only
 *   `clear()` does.
 * - Bypasses are part of the network's style: they are saved with the
 *   workspace and exported with the network until cleared.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **A bypass wins over a mapping and over the default**, for the elements
 *   it names. That is why it suits a highlight, and why it must be removed.
 * - **Use the batch call.** `setBypasses` checks every property and every id
 *   first, and sets all or none. Nothing is left half-highlighted.
 * - **Remember what was there.** `deleteBypass` removes a bypass the user set
 *   too. `clear()` restores earlier values instead of deleting them.
 * - **Highlight the border, not the fill.** A fill bypass hides the colors
 *   of a category or numeric mapping on exactly the nodes the user is asked
 *   to look at.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't use a bypass to color every node: set a default
 *   (`style/set-style-defaults`) or a mapping.
 * - Don't select nodes to highlight them: the selection belongs to the user,
 *   and changes with the next click.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

/** A color as the host stores it: `#rrggbb`. */
export type HexColor = `#${string}`

export interface HighlightOptions {
  /** Border color. Defaults to orange. */
  color?: HexColor
  /** Border width. Defaults to 6. */
  width?: number
}

export interface Highlight {
  /** Put back the bypasses these nodes had before. */
  clear: () => ApiResult
}

const PROPERTIES = ['nodeBorderColor', 'nodeBorderWidth'] as const

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function highlightWithBypass(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'visualStyle'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  nodeIds: IdType[],
  options: HighlightOptions = {},
): ApiResult<Highlight> {
  if (nodeIds.length === 0) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_NODES', 'nodeIds is empty')
  }

  // What these nodes have now, to restore it.
  const before = new Map<string, Record<IdType, unknown>>()
  for (const vpName of PROPERTIES) {
    const read = apis.visualStyle.getBypasses(networkId, vpName)
    if (!read.success) return read
    before.set(vpName, read.data.bypasses)
  }

  const set = apis.visualStyle.setBypasses(networkId, nodeIds, {
    nodeBorderColor: options.color ?? '#e69f00',
    nodeBorderWidth: options.width ?? 6,
  })
  if (!set.success) return set

  const clear = (): ApiResult => {
    for (const vpName of PROPERTIES) {
      const earlier = before.get(vpName) ?? {}
      const unset = nodeIds.filter((id) => !(id in earlier))
      if (unset.length > 0) {
        const removed = apis.visualStyle.deleteBypass(networkId, vpName, unset)
        if (!removed.success) return removed
      }
      for (const id of nodeIds.filter((id) => id in earlier)) {
        const restored = apis.visualStyle.setBypass(
          networkId,
          vpName,
          [id],
          earlier[id] as string | number,
        )
        if (!restored.success) return restored
      }
    }
    return { success: true, data: undefined }
  }
  return { success: true, data: { clear } }
}
````

## Label nodes or edges from a column

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/style/label-from-column.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Label nodes or edges from a column
 * @aliases show labels, change label, label by column, display attribute,
 *   node label, edge label, show gene names, label mapping, passthrough
 *   mapping
 * @apis table.getColumns, visualStyle.createPassthroughMapping
 * @related style/color-by-category, style/set-style-defaults,
 *   data/join-table-by-key
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user asks for nodes (or edges) to show another column as their label:
 * a gene symbol instead of an id, a score, a type.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 * - `column` is a column of the node (or edge) table that holds one value
 *   per element, not a list.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Replaces the label mapping (`nodeLabel` or `edgeLabel`) with a
 *   passthrough mapping: each element shows its own value. Mappings record
 *   no undo entry.
 * - Changes no table data.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **It replaces the existing label.** A network made from an edge list, or
 *   by most imports, already labels nodes from `name`. To go back, run the
 *   recipe with `name`.
 * - **Numbers are shown as they are stored**: `0.123456789`, not `0.12`. To
 *   format them, write the formatted text to a `string` column and label from
 *   that.
 * - **Missing values** show the mapping's fallback: the default label as it
 *   was when the mapping was made (empty unless set). A later default does
 *   not reach them.
 * - **List columns are refused.** A passthrough mapping hands the list to
 *   the renderer as it is.
 * - **The column's type must be passed exactly**: the host refuses a mapping
 *   whose `attributeType` differs from the column's (`MI2`). The recipe reads
 *   it from the table.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't set a label bypass on every element: it does not follow the data.
 * - Don't copy the column's values into `name` to change the labels.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  AppTableType,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function labelFromColumn(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'table' | 'visualStyle'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  column: string,
  tableType: AppTableType = 'node',
): ApiResult<{ column: string; type: string }> {
  const columns = apis.table.getColumns(networkId, tableType)
  if (!columns.success) return columns
  const info = columns.data.columns.find((c) => c.name === column)
  if (info === undefined) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_COLUMN', `no ${tableType} column ${column}`)
  }
  if (info.type.startsWith('list_of_')) {
    return failure('RECIPE_COLUMN_TYPE', `${column} is a ${info.type} column`)
  }

  const mapped = apis.visualStyle.createPassthroughMapping(
    networkId,
    tableType === 'node' ? 'nodeLabel' : 'edgeLabel',
    column,
    info.type,
  )
  if (!mapped.success) return mapped
  return { success: true, data: { column, type: info.type } }
}
````

## Set the style's defaults

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/style/set-style-defaults.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Set the style's defaults
 * @aliases make every node red, change node color, change node shape, set
 *   default color, default size, background color, change the look of all
 *   nodes, style all edges
 * @apis visualStyle.setDefaults, visualStyle.getVisualProperties,
 *   visualStyle.getBypasses
 * @related style/highlight-with-bypass, style/color-by-category,
 *   style/size-nodes-by-degree
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user asks to change how all nodes or edges look, "make every node
 * red", "use round nodes", "thicker edges": that is a default, not a value
 * per element.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - `defaults` names properties of the network's style, with values of their
 *   type: a `#rrggbb` color, a number, or one of the property's names
 *   (`'ellipse'`).
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Sets each default on the network's active style, all or none.
 * - Records **no** undo entry.
 * - Returns which of the properties a mapping or bypasses still override,
 *   so the caller can tell the user why some elements did not change.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **Precedence: bypass, then mapping, then default.** After "make every
 *   node red", nodes with a bypass stay as they were: `bypassed` counts them.
 * - **A mapping hides the default from every element, not only those it
 *   lists.** Where a mapping has no value for an element (a discrete mapping
 *   without its key, a missing number), the host uses the mapping's own
 *   fallback, copied from the default when the mapping was created. Setting
 *   the default later does not change it, on 1.1.0 or 1.1.1. So with a
 *   mapping on the fill, no node turns red: `shadowedByMapping` lists such
 *   properties. Delete the mapping, or make it again after the default.
 * - **Use the batch call.** `setDefaults` checks every property and value
 *   first and applies all or none. A bad value cannot leave a half-changed
 *   style.
 * - **No undo.** To let the user go back, read the old defaults first
 *   (`getDefault`) and keep them.
 * - Property names are camelCase strings such as `'nodeBackgroundColor'`,
 *   checked by the type of `defaults`.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - **Don't set a bypass on every node** to change them all. It hides every
 *   later mapping and default on those nodes, it is saved with the network,
 *   and nodes added later do not get it. Set the default.
 * - Don't delete the user's mapping to make a default show without asking.
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
  VisualPropertyName,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

/** Property names to values, as `setDefaults` takes them. */
export type StyleDefaults = Parameters<
  CyWebApiType['visualStyle']['setDefaults']
>[1]

export interface DefaultsSet {
  /** Properties whose default a mapping overrides. */
  shadowedByMapping: VisualPropertyName[]
  /** Elements whose bypass overrides the default, per property. */
  bypassed: Partial<Record<VisualPropertyName, number>>
}

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function setStyleDefaults(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'visualStyle'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  defaults: StyleDefaults,
): ApiResult<DefaultsSet> {
  const names = Object.keys(defaults) as VisualPropertyName[]
  if (names.length === 0) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_DEFAULTS', 'defaults is empty')
  }

  const set = apis.visualStyle.setDefaults(networkId, defaults)
  if (!set.success) return set

  const properties = apis.visualStyle.getVisualProperties(networkId)
  if (!properties.success) return properties
  const mapped = new Set(
    properties.data.properties.filter((p) => p.hasMapping).map((p) => p.name),
  )

  const result: DefaultsSet = { shadowedByMapping: [], bypassed: {} }
  for (const name of names) {
    if (mapped.has(name)) result.shadowedByMapping.push(name)
    const bypasses = apis.visualStyle.getBypasses(networkId, name)
    if (!bypasses.success) return bypasses
    const count = Object.keys(bypasses.data.bypasses).length
    if (count > 0) result.bypassed[name] = count
  }
  return { success: true, data: result }
}
````

## Size nodes by their degree

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web-app-examples/46ebe17ac64421060983dcc2db9a2f9a37cea28a/cookbook/recipes/style/size-nodes-by-degree.ts

````typescript
/**
 * @recipe Size nodes by their degree
 * @aliases size by degree, bigger nodes for hubs, node size by connections,
 *   scale nodes, hubs larger, node size mapping, size by number of edges
 * @apis element.getNodeIds, element.getEdges, table.getColumns,
 *   table.createColumn, table.setValues, visualStyle.createContinuousMapping,
 *   visualStyle.deleteMapping
 * @related data/add-computed-column, style/color-nodes-by-numeric-column,
 *   style/color-by-category
 *
 * ## When to use
 *
 * The user asks for well-connected nodes to look bigger: the size of each
 * node grows with its number of edges.
 *
 * ## Preconditions
 *
 * - The network's data is loaded; see `events/follow-current-network`.
 * - Not every node has the same degree.
 *
 * ## Side effects
 *
 * - Writes each node's degree to an `integer` column (default `degree`),
 *   creating it if there is none: **one** undo entry for the values, none for
 *   the column.
 * - Replaces any mapping on node width and node height with a continuous
 *   mapping from that column. Mappings record no undo entry.
 * - If the second mapping fails, the recipe deletes the first again; the
 *   column keeps its values.
 *
 * ## Pitfalls
 *
 * - **A mapping reads a column, not the topology.** So the degree is written
 *   to the table first. The sizes follow the column, and the column does not
 *   follow later edits: run the recipe again after adding or deleting edges.
 * - **Missing values.** A node without a value gets the mapping's fallback,
 *   the default size when the mapping was made. Every node gets a value here;
 *   a node added later has none until the recipe runs again.
 * - **Non-numeric values.** A degree is always a whole number. An existing
 *   column of that name in another type is refused.
 * - **An empty network** has no degree to map: `RECIPE_NO_NODES`.
 * - **All values equal**, a ring or a grid, leaves no range to scale:
 *   `RECIPE_SINGLE_VALUE`, before anything is written. Set one default size
 *   instead (`style/set-style-defaults`).
 * - **Map width and height both.** Mapping one makes ellipses.
 * - **Column names and case** are checked as in `data/add-computed-column`:
 *   a name that differs from an existing column only by case is refused on
 *   both releases.
 * - **Find the range with a loop.** `Math.min(...values)` throws a
 *   `RangeError` past about 120,000 values.
 *
 * ## Don't
 *
 * - Don't set a width bypass on every node: it does not follow the data, and
 *   it hides any later mapping.
 * - Don't pass `attributeType: 'double'` for an `integer` column: the host
 *   refuses it (`MI2`).
 *
 * ## Wiring
 *
 * Host-wide: `apis` may come from any call site. See `wiring/from-mount.ts`,
 * `wiring/from-apps-menu.ts`, `wiring/from-panel.tsx` and
 * `wiring/from-window.ts`.
 */
import type {
  ApiFailure,
  ApiResult,
  CellEdit,
  CyWebApiType,
  IdType,
} from 'cyweb/ApiTypes'

export interface SizeOptions {
  /** The column the degree is written to. Defaults to `degree`. */
  column?: string
  /** Size of the least connected nodes. Defaults to 20. */
  smallest?: number
  /** Size of the most connected nodes. Defaults to 80. */
  largest?: number
}

const failure = (code: string, message: string): ApiFailure => ({
  success: false,
  error: { code, severity: 'error', message },
})

export function sizeNodesByDegree(
  apis: Pick<CyWebApiType, 'element' | 'table' | 'visualStyle'>,
  networkId: IdType,
  options: SizeOptions = {},
): ApiResult<{ min: number; max: number }> {
  const column = options.column ?? 'degree'
  const smallest = options.smallest ?? 20
  const largest = options.largest ?? 80

  const nodes = apis.element.getNodeIds(networkId)
  if (!nodes.success) return nodes
  const edges = apis.element.getEdges(networkId)
  if (!edges.success) return edges
  if (nodes.data.nodeIds.length === 0) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NO_NODES', 'the network has no node')
  }

  const degree = new Map<IdType, number>()
  for (const id of nodes.data.nodeIds) degree.set(id, 0)
  for (const edge of edges.data.edges) {
    degree.set(edge.sourceId, (degree.get(edge.sourceId) ?? 0) + 1)
    degree.set(edge.targetId, (degree.get(edge.targetId) ?? 0) + 1)
  }
  let min = Infinity
  let max = -Infinity
  for (const value of degree.values()) {
    min = Math.min(min, value)
    max = Math.max(max, value)
  }
  if (min === max) {
    return failure(
      'RECIPE_SINGLE_VALUE',
      `every node has degree ${min}; there is nothing to scale`,
    )
  }

  const columns = apis.table.getColumns(networkId, 'node')
  if (!columns.success) return columns
  const same = columns.data.columns.find(
    (c) => c.name.toLowerCase() === column.toLowerCase(),
  )
  if (same !== undefined && same.name !== column) {
    return failure('RECIPE_NAME_CLASH', `a column named ${same.name} exists`)
  }
  if (same !== undefined && same.type !== 'integer' && same.type !== 'long') {
    return failure('RECIPE_COLUMN_TYPE', `${column} is a ${same.type} column`)
  }
  if (same === undefined) {
    const made = apis.table.createColumn(networkId, 'node', column, 'integer', 0)
    if (!made.success) return made
  }
  const edits: CellEdit[] = []
  for (const [id, value] of degree) edits.push({ id, column, value })
  const written = apis.table.setValues(networkId, 'node', edits)
  if (!written.success) return written

  const sizeBy = (vpName: 'nodeWidth' | 'nodeHeight'): ApiResult =>
    apis.visualStyle.createContinuousMapping(networkId, vpName, {
      vpType: 'number',
      attribute: column,
      attributeType: same?.type ?? 'integer',
      attributeValues: [min, max],
      controlPoints: [
        { value: min, vpValue: smallest },
        { value: max, vpValue: largest },
      ],
      ltMinVpValue: smallest,
      gtMaxVpValue: largest,
    })
  const width = sizeBy('nodeWidth')
  if (!width.success) return width
  const height = sizeBy('nodeHeight')
  if (!height.success) {
    apis.visualStyle.deleteMapping(networkId, 'nodeWidth')
    return height
  }
  return { success: true, data: { min, max } }
}
````

# API reference

- App API reference, as of Cytoscape Web 1.1.0: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cytoscape/cytoscape-web/6619411b3e4f4367679cd69299c63abdb865121c/src/app-api/api_docs/Api.md
